correctness.rationale: For upsets U, Diamond p is D(U)={w: all v>=w all A in N(v) meet U} and Box top is stable-world set S={s: all t>=s N(t) nonempty}. If SNDR holds, any A disjoint from U at v>=w admits B contained in down A at some stable s>=w, so implication Box top -> Diamond p fails there and I_Diamond holds at w; if SNDR fails, U=W\down A is an upset falsifying I_Diamond at witness w. This proves exact arbitrary nonempty preorder correspondence including empty families and infinite W. For labelled chains, rank(A)=-1 for empty, otherwise max A; the last empty row and least suffix rank yield exact sum over ell,m. The n=1,2 direct Kripke truth-table evaluation produced C1=4,C2=241; independently evaluated formula gives C1=4,C2=241,C3=16690673,C4=18446303034659832065. Strict 3-world counterexample N(0)={{2}}, N(1)=empty family, N(2)={{0}} satisfies SNDR but not continual support; earlier sizes cannot. Large counts are exact integer evaluation of an algebraic formula, not proof by finite search.
